title: The Rich King and the Vault of Gold

keywords: the angel of death and the rich king
full_text:
A wealthy king of the East spent thirty years amassing all the gold, diamonds, and precious pearls of his empire into a colossal subterranean vault beneath his fortress. The vault was constructed of solid stone with an iron door that locked with an intricate mechanism of twenty-four hidden tumblers.

One morning, the king entered his vault alone, carrying no candle, intending to gloat over his immense mounds of glittering coin. The heavy iron door, caught by a sudden draft, swung shut behind him with a thunderous clang! The intricate lock snapped into place.

The king smiled, unconcerned, reached into his sash for the master key—only to realize with icy horror that he had left the key hanging on the peg outside in his bedchamber!

He shouted for his guards, but the walls were ten feet thick, and no sound could penetrate the stone. He beat upon the iron portal with his fists until his hands were bruised and bloody, but the fortress remained silent.

Days passed in pitch-black darkness. His throat burned with intolerable thirst, and his stomach gnawed with agonizing hunger. Surrounding him were three million gold dinars, heaps of emeralds, and chests of rubies, yet there was not a single drop of water or a crumb of dry bread.

In his final hours, realizing the utter vanity of his life, the dying king dipped his finger into his own blood and wrote upon the iron wall of the vault:
'Here perished a monarch who possessed three million dinars of gold,
Yet could not purchase a cup of clear water or a crust of bread;
Learn, O traveler of the future, that true wealth lies in what you give,
Not in the cold stone where your greed buries your soul!'

When the guards finally forced the vault open weeks later, they found the lifeless king lying upon his gold, reading his tragic inscription, which was engraved upon the city gates as an eternal warning against greed.
moral: Gold hoarded in cold vaults cannot purchase a single moment of life or a crust of bread in the hour of need.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Angel of Death and the Rich King"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
